Paula and Gregory Chow Institute for Studies in Economics (Chow Institute) invites applications for either tenure-track or tenured full-time faculty positions in the upcoming academic year, starting in September 2027.

(Prepared by Professor Ben Bernanke, Chair of the Department of Economics, Princeton University, in May 2001.)

Gregory C. Chow is the Class of 1913 Professor of Political Economy Emeritus at Princeton University. He has been a major figure in econometrics and applied economics. Every beginning econometrics student learns the "Chow test", a statistical test for structural change in a regression. However, Gregory's work extends far beyond his eponymous test. He was a major figure in the postwar flowering of econometrics, and his applied work included important research in microeconomics, macroeconomics, and development economics (particularly in reference to Southeast Asia).

Gregory has become a towering figure in economic transition and economics education in Asia. He played an important role in the transformation of the economy of mainland China. Gregory also did a great deal for ties between China and the United States, including supporting education programs for Chinese students in both countries. His experiences and writings on China were the basis for a popular undergraduate course on the Chinese economy that Gregory taught regularly at Princeton for many years.

Chow Institute is devoted to excellence in training academic candidates, producing original research, and facilitating dialogue of strong policy relevance.

XMU-CAS Basic Science Center for Econometric Modelling and Economic Policy Studies is jointly managed by Chow Institute and the Center for Forecasting Science at Chinese Academy of Sciences. Approved in 2019, the Basic Science Center is the first national basic science center project not only in the Management Science Division of National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), but also in Fujian Province and Xiamen University. It is positioned to be an academic highland for econometric modeling and economic forecasting with international influence.

MOE Key Laboratory of Econometrics (Xiamen University) is among one of the first key laboratories of the Ministry of Education (MOE) founded in 2009. As China's first key laboratory in Economics, the Key Lab strives to promote econometrics education, research and international academic exchanges in Xiamen University and China.

XMU Center for Macroeconomic Research was established in September 2001 with a specific research agenda focusing on policy relevance. Since February 2005, the center has become a key research base in humanities and social sciences of the Ministry of Education. It is also one of the most important components of the National Philosophy and Social Science Innovation Base, and has long been engaging in China's macroeconomic analysis and forecasting research.

The Faculty of Business, Economics, and Social Sciences invites applications for the position of a Full Professor (W3) of Household Finance at the Institute of Financial Management to be filled in the winter semester 2027/28.

The successful candidate will be appointed as Full Professor and will represent the field of Household Finance in both research and teaching. The position offers an excellent opportunity to advance an independent research agenda in a dynamic and growing area of finance and to contribute to the continued development of the Faculty’s established Finance profile. Attractive opportunities for collaboration exist, particularly with chairs in Finance, Economics, and Data Science, as well as with related areas such as Business and Economics Education, Business Psychology, and Communication Science.

In research, candidates are expected to have an internationally visible profile in Household Finance, demonstrated by relevant publications in leading international journals. Their research agenda should contribute to the international Household Finance literature and be strongly empirical and quantitative in orientation. Particular emphasis is placed on expertise in microeconometric methods, causal inference, survey and experimental designs, panel data, digital behavioral data, and/or machine-learning-based analytical methods. Experience with, or clear potential for, acquiring competitive third-party funding is expected.

Possible research areas include, but are not limited to:
	Saving, investment, pension, and borrowing decisions of households
	Financial literacy, financial inclusion, and financial resilience
	Behavioral determinants of household financial decision-making
	Subjective expectations, risk perceptions, and information processing by households
	Wealth accumulation, investment behavior, and financial inequality
	Digital finance, FinTech, and algorithm-supported financial decision-making from a household perspective
	Sustainable investment decisions by households and sustainable financial products

This may include, but is not limited to, fields such as international economics, development economics, behavioral economics, labor economics, political economy, and applied microeconomics and macroeconomics. Applicants should demonstrate a strong research profile, evidenced by a substantial record of high-quality research accomplishments or, for more junior candidates, clear evidence of the potential to develop such a record. Candidates should also have an ambitious and active research agenda and a strong record of teaching excellence.

Appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, depending on the candidate’s experience and qualifications.

Qualifications

 A Ph.D. in Economics.
 A strong and active research agenda, with a demonstrated record of publication in leading economics journals or, for junior candidates, clear evidence of the potential to establish such a record.
 A strong commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring, demonstrated through previous teaching experience and, for senior candidates, a sustained record of teaching effectiveness and student mentorship.

Faculty typically teach two courses (or 6 credit hours) per semester (a 2-2 load), supported by best-in-class instructional infrastructure.

 Access to GU-Q faculty research funds.
 Eligibility for funding through the Qatar Research, Development, and Innovation Council (QRDI).

 Generous conference travel funding and professional development resources.

 Fully furnished, high-quality housing.
 Transportation allowance.
 Annual family home leave.
 Worldwide health insurance coverage.

GU-Q is an integral part of Georgetown University, delivering the renowned School of Foreign Service’s Bachelor of Science in Foreign Service (BSFS) degree.
